verdict.rationale: Nitrokey's own shop page says the Nitrokey 3 includes a Common Criteria EAL 6+ certified secure element. That is a component-level certification, not evidence that the whole device is FIPS 140 validated or CC certified. Nothing in the pack documents water or crush resistance, and one hands-on user calls a Nitrokey U2F key flimsy. missing for 10: device-level FIPS 140 validation or Common Criteria product certification, documented water/crush resistance or other durability ratings, independent corroboration of certification status.

support.subject: As an IT admin, certified models exist for regulated environments — FIPS 140 validated or Common Criteria certified — with documented durability (water/crush resistance)

citations.quote: Common Criteria EAL 6+ certified secure element
